context_requirements: Intact downstream calcium and stress-response signaling
Proliferating cells may show stronger secondary antiproliferative effects
falsifiers: No consistent transcriptional changes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Changes that are indistinguishable from vehicle or from generic stress responses across all lines
Lack of dose-dependent or target-dependent effects when compared with sigma receptor antagonists

evidence.supports: Sigma receptor agonists modulate cell death and signaling in neural cells, suggesting potential transcriptional effects
Sigma receptor ligands affect oxidative stress, ER stress, and apoptosis pathways in vitro

changes: Removed GRIN1, GRIN2A, GRIN2B from primary_targets: sigma receptor agonists do not directly target NMDA receptor subunits; the cited abstracts concern sigma receptor modulation, not NMDA receptor agonism.
Removed NMDA receptor subunit expression from context_requirements for the same reason.
Kept direction assignments: stress/oxidative-response genes up and proliferation genes down are consistent with sigma receptor agonist-induced stress and antiproliferative effects.
Kept kinetics and magnitude as plausible for a slow, weak-to-moderate transcriptional response.
Kept line responses as no line-specific data contradict them.
Kept both evidence citations; their abstracts support sigma receptor ligand effects on oxidative stress, ER stress, apoptosis, and signaling.
